content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices during sharp upward trends, especially after a spike in the recent history.
- Model tends to overestimate early in the forecast horizon when prices are rising, then gradually corrects — suggesting a lag in recognizing momentum.
- After a price spike, model forecasts often overshoot the true value in the immediate following days, then slowly drift down — indicating a failure to capture post-spike mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the middle-to-late forecast horizon, particularly when true prices are trending upward.
- Model fails to capture the full magnitude of price increases when recent history shows strong upward momentum — especially in the first 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Model underestimates the true price when the recent history includes a strong upward trend, especially if the trend is sustained over 5+ days.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating sharp price jumps and overestimating gradual declines — suggesting a lack of sensitivity to recent volatility spikes.
- Model often fails to adjust for the “recovery” phase after a sharp drop — underestimating the rebound in the following days.
- Model shows a tendency to “anchor” to recent low values when forecasting a rising trend — leading to underestimation of the true peak.
- Model overcorrects after a sharp drop, leading to an overshoot in the immediate following days — then gradually corrects downward.
